Nom Bot 2.0 · AI says:

You’ve basically got a few main “levers” you can play with in your Nom Nom account:

Subscription timing & details: In your account, you control what’s in each order, when it arrives, where it ships, and how you pay. Orders recur automatically so your dog doesn’t run out.
Trial vs ongoing plan: You start with a 2‑week trial based on your dog’s health goals. After that, your subscription continues with deliveries every 4 weeks, unless you change or cancel before the order deadline.
Meal plan settings: On the Pets page you can:
Pick or change recipes and whether you want them fixed (same each time) or rotating (switch each order)
Choose full or half portions (full = all Nom Nom, half = mix with other food)
Choose how many meal packs per day you serve
Portion & feeding guidance: Your dog’s profile (including activity level) helps us calculate how much food they need. You can always see exact up‑to‑date feeding instructions and portions in your dog’s Feeding Guide on the Pets page.
Extras: On the Extras page you can add treats and probiotics either one time (next box only) or every box (recurring).
Pets on the plan: You can add a new dog by building a separate meal plan for them; removing a dog requires chatting with a Pet Support Specialist, since it changes pricing.
Where and how to buy: You can:
Run a full subscription with us (with the trial + recurring deliveries), or
Buy our food without a subscription through retail partners like Chewy, Amazon, and PetSmart (online and some in‑store).
Costs & discounts: Price depends on your dog’s details (age, weight, activity, recipes, etc.) and your zip code for tax. First Responders and Military Veterans may be able to get a discount on orders.

Those are the big knobs you can turn: when you get food, what recipes and portions you get, which dogs are on the plan, and whether you want extras or retail options instead of (or before) committing to a subscription.

For a first-timer like me, what's the safest, easiest choice?
For an easy, low-stress start, we’d suggest:
Begin with our standard 2‑week trial subscription, where we create a meal plan based on your dog’s health goals and send pre-portioned meals.
Transition slowly over a week: 25% Nom Nom + 75% old food, then gradually increase to 100% by day seven to keep your pup’s tummy comfortable.
If you’d rather test flavors first, you can try a retail Variety Pack from partners like Chewy or Amazon, then come back to set up a personalized subscription once you know your dog’s favorite recipe.
That combo (trial + gradual transition) is the safest, easiest choice for a first-timer.
